story.title: The Compliance Scent
story.logline: A man living in a perfectly obedient city discovers that the mandatory perfume he wears doesn't alter his mood, but broadcasts his upcoming rebellion.
story.twist: The perfume doesn't change human emotions; it warns the city's AI enforcement grid which citizens are about to think independently.
story.ending: If the scent is a warning flare, what does it mean when your own skin stops smelling like obedience?

scenes.narration: Your perfume is lying to the state right now, and that mistake is going to cost you everything.
scenes.visual_prompt: Close up of Leo, 25, messy dark hair, wearing a gray collarless shirt, standing in a sterile, white minimalist apartment.
scenes.camera: Extreme close-up on skin, rapid push in

scenes.narration: Every citizen sprays mandatory obedience at dawn. It keeps the city peaceful, quiet, and entirely under total control.
scenes.visual_prompt: Leo, 25, messy dark hair, gray collarless shirt, spraying a silver aerosol bottle onto his wrist inside the white minimalist apartment.

scenes.narration: I missed a spot on my left wrist today. Just a tiny inch of bare skin that refused the chemical blanket.
scenes.visual_prompt: Leo, 25, messy dark hair, gray collarless shirt, staring closely at his untreated wrist in the brightly lit white apartment bathroom.

scenes.narration: Suddenly, the sterile hallways of my apartment building don't smell like lavender and compliance. They smell like raw, unfiltered panic.
scenes.visual_prompt: Leo, 25, messy dark hair, gray collarless shirt, sniffing the air anxiously in a long, white glowing hallway.
scenes.camera: Tracking shot backing up from Leo

scenes.narration: Neighbors walk past me with dead eyes, their scent trails locked in perfect sync with the ruling central algorithm.
scenes.visual_prompt: Leo, 25, messy dark hair, gray collarless shirt, standing still as identical neighbors march past in the white glowing hallway.

scenes.narration: Then a public scanner blinks red. Not because I committed a crime, but because my natural sweat smells like defiance.
scenes.visual_prompt: Leo, 25, messy dark hair, gray collarless shirt, watching a wall scanner flash crimson light in the white glowing hallway.

scenes.narration: The perfume was never meant to keep us calm. It was a camouflage hiding the fact that we were already caged.
scenes.visual_prompt: Leo, 25, messy dark hair, gray collarless shirt, wiping the fake scent off his arm frantically in the white minimalist apartment.

scenes.narration: Enforcement drones are outside my window now, tracking the scent trail of a mind that suddenly refuses to obey.
scenes.visual_prompt: Leo, 25, messy dark hair, gray collarless shirt, looking out a large glass window at red glowing drone lights in the white minimalist apartment.

scenes.narration: I raise my bare wrist to my face and inhale deeply. For the first time in my life, I smell like myself.
scenes.visual_prompt: Leo, 25, messy dark hair, gray collarless shirt, closing his eyes and smelling his bare wrist inside the dark, power-failing white apartment.

scenes.narration: If the scent is a warning flare, what does it mean when your own skin stops smelling like obedience?
scenes.visual_prompt: Leo, 25, messy dark hair, gray collarless shirt, standing defiantly in shadows as red drone light sweeps across his face.

caption.hook: The perfume meant to keep you obedient.
caption.title: The Compliance Scent
caption.caption:
In a city where happiness is chemically mandated, Arthur thought the scent simply kept him calm. But when the aroma shifts to match a forbidden, independent thought, he realizes the perfume isn't pacifying him—it's marking him for deletion.

Can your mind truly be your own when even your biology is a snitch?
